title: Writing: A Discussion Essay on Public Health Responsibility

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the debate: should responsibility for health lie with governments or individuals?
writingModel.hint: Present both sides — do not state your opinion yet

writingModel.placeholder: Case for government responsibility: public health, prevention, reducing inequality
writingModel.hint: Use quantifiers: "all citizens", "few individuals", "a great deal of evidence"

writingModel.placeholder: Case for individual responsibility: personal freedom, lifestyle choices, accountability
writingModel.hint: Use "on the other hand," "however," "neither extreme is correct"

writingModel.placeholder: Balanced conclusion: both play a role — what is the right balance?
writingModel.hint: Use "on balance," "both governments and individuals," "neither alone is sufficient"

writingTemplate.suffix: is a matter of continuing debate.
writingTemplate.placeholder: responsibility for public health lies with governments or individuals
writingTemplate.hint: Introduce the topic without taking sides

writingTemplate.prefix: Those who argue for greater government responsibility point out that
writingTemplate.placeholder: many health outcomes are determined by social and environmental factors beyond individual control
writingTemplate.hint: Present the strongest argument for this position

writingTemplate.prefix: Furthermore, a great deal of evidence suggests that
writingTemplate.placeholder: preventive public health measures reduce costs and save lives
writingTemplate.hint: "A great deal of evidence" = formal quantifier; use a specific example

writingTemplate.placeholder: individual choices — diet, exercise, sleep — play a crucial role that no government can control

writingTemplate.prefix: Critics of heavy intervention argue that
writingTemplate.placeholder: excessive government control of lifestyle choices undermines personal freedom
writingTemplate.hint: Present this concern without dismissing it

writingTemplate.prefix: On balance, I believe that neither governments nor individuals can
writingTemplate.suffix: alone — both have essential roles to play.

items: All citizens deserve access to basic healthcare.
Many health inequalities are structural, not personal.
A great deal of evidence supports investment in preventive medicine.
Few individuals can control environmental factors alone.
The majority of preventable deaths could be avoided with public health investment.
Each person has the right to make their own lifestyle choices.
Neither taxes nor regulation can substitute for personal motivation.
A large number of health conditions are directly linked to personal habits.
Both diet and exercise are within most individuals' control.
Every adult bears some responsibility for their own wellbeing.
Neither extreme tells the whole story.
Both governments and individuals have essential roles.
A little government intervention goes a long way.
While few would argue against personal responsibility, structural factors cannot be ignored.
All sides of this debate have merit.
A great deal of research suggests…
A large number of studies confirm…
The majority of evidence points to…
Plenty of data supports the view that…
Little credible evidence exists for…

questions.text: "___ citizens deserve access to quality healthcare." (100%, as a group)
"___ evidence suggests that preventive medicine is cost-effective." (large formal amount)
questions.hint: "A great deal of" = formal, large amount + uncountable

questions.text: "___ governments ___ individuals can solve public health alone." (not one, not the other)
questions.hint: "Neither... nor" = not one and not the other

questions.text: "___ studies have found a clear link between loneliness and poor health." (large number, formal)
questions.hint: "A large number of" = formal equivalent of "many" (countable)

questions.text: "There is ___ credible evidence for the claim that supplements prevent disease." (almost none, negative)
"A few studies support this view" is more positive than "few studies support this view."
"___ side of this debate is completely wrong — both contain important truths."
questions.hint: "Neither" = not one and not the other (of two sides)

questions.text: "___ of the arguments presented were convincing." (positive — some were convincing)
